answer: An agent economy can make influence proportional to value locked in a time-delayed bond, rather than to the number of accounts. Each agent’s bond backs its actions; if an independent challenge reveals copied credentials or coordinated identities, the bond is slashed and the result’s influence is reduced. A new identity therefore cannot simply echo a trusted agent’s reputation: it must tie up fresh capital and wait through the challenge window. The ripple of coordinated failures can expose linked accounts, while a falcon account gains no advantage unless it risks real funds too.
